result.title: EvoBelief: Falsifiable World Models for Self-Improving LLM Agents
result.summary: Self-evolving LLM agents typically improve how they act through accumulated experience, reflection, or skills. Yet even procedurally capable agents can fail when their beliefs about environment dynamics are incomplete, incorrect, or outdated. We study a complementary axis of self-evolution: evolving those beliefs during deployment. Such beliefs can support multiple tasks, but incorrect ones can also propagate across them. We introduce EvoBelief, a self-evolving world model that represents environment knowledge as falsifiable hypotheses. Unexpected outcomes and decision-relevant unknowns trigger hypothesis formation. Later observations and controlled experiments provide independent validation before a rule can guide predictions or plans within its supported scope. Counterexamples narrow or retire rules as the environment changes. The language model remains frozen, and each rule remains linked to its evidence and the decisions it changes. Across four benchmarks spanning static dynamics, hidden drift, and scientific discovery, EvoBelief improves task performance and reuses learned rules across tasks. On ALFWorld without actor-side transition memory, it improves success over the matched Frozen World Model by 23.9% and 31.3% with Claude Haiku 4.5 and GPT-5.4, respectively. On MiniGrid, it revises stale rules and recovers after unannounced dynamics changes. In DiscoveryWorld's Reactor Lab, it discovers and validates quantitative laws, completing 83.3% of Normal-tier and 58.3% of Challenge-tier instances, versus 0% for each evaluated baseline. These results demonstrate self-improvement through testable, revisable environment knowledge rather than model-parameter updates.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EvoBelief：把 LLM 智能体对环境动态的知识表示为可证伪假设，由意外结果与决策相关未知触发假设生成，经后续观察或受控实验独立验证后才允许指导预测与规划，反例则收窄或淘汰规则，语言模型参数保持冻结。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「假设—证据绑定—反例修订」的信念状态维护方式，可能与 LVR 中何时更新内部状态、如何用视觉证据校验 latent 内容并决定停止推理有可供核查的联系；但该工作面向文本化智能体世界模型，未涉及视觉 latent 表示。
